raw_case_text:
A 19-year-old previously healthy Hispanic female presented with chief complaint of progressively worsening shortness of breath and heart palpitations for 1 week. She had previously recently been evaluated at an outside hospital without imaging and was diagnosed with gastritis, then discharged home. Prior medical history was positive for childhood asthma and removal of a lipoma from her right flank. There was no family history of heart disease, but she did note a paternal aunt with a history of unspecified mediastinal cancer. The patient emigrated to the United States from Mexico 2 years ago and had visited Mexico 2 months prior to presentation. She had never been pregnant and was not sexually active. She denied smoking, alcohol or drug use. On presentation, her vital signs were blood pressure 128/84, pulse 111 beats per minute, respiration rate 12 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation 100% on room air. She appeared comfortable. Cardiovascular exam revealed normal rate and rhythm, grade 1 mid-frequency ejection murmur at left upper sternal border, normal upper extremity pulses and decreased lower extremity pulses. Blood pressure of right arm was 140/88, left arm was 136/90, right leg was 105/67 and left leg was 82/58. The remainder of the physical exam was normal.
Chest X-ray showed a right peri-hilar mass with some tracheal compression (Fig. 1). Computed tomography (CT) scan revealed a 1.2 x 1.1 cm mass in the right hilar region with associated diffuse mediastinal lymphadenopathy (Fig. 2). A previously undiagnosed severe isthmic coarctation of the aorta was noted immediately distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery with surrounding collateral arteries. Coarctation was confirmed with echocardiogram that showed peak gradient around 40 mm Hg. Systolic function was normal. Initial imaging was suspicious for malignancy or infectious process. There was concern that the coarctation may be related to the mediastinal process. Initial bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) and fine-needle aspiration (FNA) were non-diagnostic. Subsequent endobronchial ultrasound (EBUS) with trans-bronchial needle biopsy of the mediastinal lymph nodes showed coalescing fibrocaseous granulomas with necrosis (Fig. 3, 4). Gram stain, culture and acid-fast bacilli (AFB) stain were negative. QuantiFERON gold test was also negative. Serology was positive for Histoplasma (titer 1:256). Pathologic analysis showed necrotizing granulomas with small fungal yeast that was morphologically most consistent with Histoplasma (Fig. 5).
Repeat CT chest revealed pericardial thickening with massive pericardial effusion (Fig. 6). There was 2 cm pericardial thickening that was confirmed with echocardiogram. Emergent pericardiocentesis was required and 260 cc of yellow blood-tinged fluid was removed, then a pericardial drain was placed. The patient was treated initially with amphotericin B. Due to allergic reaction, she was transitioned to voriconazole. Surgical repair of the coarctation of the aorta was delayed until resolution of the Histoplasma infection. She eventually underwent surgical coarctectomy with end-to-end anastomosis with good results.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 19-year-old Hispanic female presented with a 1-week history of progressively worsening shortness of breath and heart palpitations.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Previously healthy 19-year-old female presented with 1 week of progressive dyspnea and palpitations after a recent outside hospital visit where she had been diagnosed clinically with gastritis without imaging.
subjective.past_medical_history: Childhood asthma and right flank lipoma excision. Family/epidemiological/social history: Paternal aunt with unspecified mediastinal cancer, no family history of heart disease; emigrated from Mexico to the US 2 years prior and visited Mexico 2 months before presentation; nulligravid, not sexually active, and denied tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for worsening shortness of breath and palpitations.

objective.physical_examination: Vital signs: BP 128/84 mmHg (right arm 140/88, left arm 136/90, right leg 105/67, left leg 82/58 mmHg), HR 111 bpm, RR 12 breaths/min, SpO2 100% on room air; comfortable appearance. Cardiovascular: normal rate and rhythm, grade 1 mid-frequency ejection murmur at the left upper sternal border, normal upper extremity pulses, and diminished lower extremity pulses. Remainder of exam normal.
objective.routine_investigations: QuantiFERON-TB Gold test: negative. Histoplasma serology: positive at titer 1:256. Chest X-ray: right perihilar mass with mild tracheal compression. Echocardiogram: confirmed aortic coarctation with peak gradient ~40 mmHg and normal systolic function; repeat echocardiogram confirmed 2 cm pericardial thickening and massive pericardial effusion.
objective.advanced_workup: CT chest: 1.2 x 1.1 cm right hilar mass with diffuse mediastinal lymphadenopathy, severe isthmic coarctation of the aorta immediately distal to the left subclavian artery with collateral vessels, and on repeat CT, 2 cm pericardial thickening with massive pericardial effusion. Initial bronchoscopy with BAL and FNA: non-diagnostic. Endobronchial ultrasound (EBUS) with transbronchial needle biopsy of mediastinal lymph nodes: coalescing fibrocaseous necrotizing granulomas containing small fungal yeast morphologically consistent with Histoplasma (Gram stain, culture, and AFB stain negative).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Mediastinal histoplasmosis complicated by massive pericardial effusion/pericarditis and newly diagnosed severe isthmic coarctation of the aorta. Confirmation: EBUS-guided mediastinal lymph node biopsy showing necrotizing fibrocaseous granulomas with small yeast forms consistent with Histoplasma and positive Histoplasma serology (titer 1:256). Plan & clinical course: Underwent emergent pericardiocentesis (260 mL yellow blood-tinged fluid removed) and pericardial drain placement, and initiated amphotericin B followed by transition to voriconazole due to an allergic reaction; following resolution of the Histoplasma infection, she underwent successful surgical coarctectomy with end-to-end anastomosis.
